## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Pañcuposathikajātaka* (Ja 490) is a canonical birth-story included in the Jātaka section of the Khuddaka Nikāya [SuttaCentral]. According to the narrative framework recorded on SuttaCentral, the Buddha delivered the teaching while dwelling at Jetavana before five hundred lay followers who had undertaken the sabbath vows (*uposatha*) [SuttaCentral]. Observing that the day's teaching would concern these laymen, the Buddha confirmed their observance and praised it, noting that the sabbath was anciently maintained by the wise in order to master passion and lust; at their request, he then related a narrative of the past opening with the verse phrase "Thou art content" [SuttaCentral].
